name: M.Sc. (Agriculture) Agronomy
duration_note: University regulations based on the ICAR framework commonly allow up to 5 academic years (10 semesters) to complete the degree; the exact maximum is set by each university.

hero.summary: A two-year master's degree on how field crops are grown, fed, watered and protected from weeds, built on ICAR's restructured postgraduate syllabus. Students combine advanced coursework in crop, soil, water and weed management with a supervised thesis based on field or pot experiments.

overview.heading: What an M.Sc. in Agronomy covers
paragraphs: Agronomy is the branch of agricultural science that deals with producing crops efficiently on a given piece of land: choosing crops and cropping systems, managing nutrients and irrigation, controlling weeds and conserving soil. At master's level in India, the programme is normally offered by state agricultural universities, ICAR deemed universities and central agricultural universities, as well as some private universities that follow the ICAR syllabus.

Under ICAR's Broad Subject Matter Area (BSMA) restructured curriculum, a master's student completes 70 credits: 20 in major (agronomy) courses, 8 in a minor subject, 6 in supporting courses such as statistics, 5 in common courses, a 1-credit seminar and 30 credits of thesis research. Core agronomy courses include modern concepts in crop production, soil fertility and nutrient management, weed management and water management.

The revised syllabus also adds newer topics such as conservation agriculture, precision farming, protected and soilless cultivation, and the use of GIS, GPS and remote sensing. Course codes, elective menus and the minor subjects available differ from one university to another.

highlights.label: Typical entry degree
highlights.value: B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture or an accepted allied four-year degree

highlights.label: National entrance
highlights.value: ICAR AIEEA (PG), conducted by NTA, Agronomy subject group

highlights.label: Next step
highlights.value: Ph.D. Agronomy (ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF or university entrance)

who_should_apply: Agriculture graduates who enjoyed field crop production, farming systems and on-farm experiments during the undergraduate programme
Students comfortable spending long periods on research farms, recording crop observations across a season
Applicants interested in water, nutrient and weed management problems faced by farmers in their region
Those planning a research, teaching or extension career, or a Ph.D. in crop science
Learners willing to use statistics and data tools to design and analyse experiments

curriculum.heading: Course structure under the ICAR restructured syllabus
curriculum.intro: The programme follows ICAR's credit framework: core and elective agronomy courses, a minor from a related department, supporting statistics courses, common research-skills courses and a thesis. Course titles below come from a university syllabus prepared as per BSMA; subject names, codes and electives vary by university, so check your admitting university's course catalogue.

structure.focus: Compulsory courses that cover the scientific basis of crop production and input management.
courses: Principles and Practices of Soil Fertility and Nutrient Management
Principles and Practices of Weed Management
Principles and Practices of Water Management

structure.focus: Electives on specific crop groups and production systems, chosen with the advisory committee.
courses: Agronomy of Major Cereals and Pulses
Agronomy of Oilseed, Fibre and Sugar Crops
Agronomy of Fodder and Forage Crops
Principles and Practices of Organic Farming

structure.focus: Related subjects such as soil science and plant physiology, plus statistics for designing and analysing experiments.
courses: Management of Problem Soils and Waters
Plant Water Relations and Mineral Nutrition

structure.focus: Research-skills courses common to all master's students, one seminar and a 30-credit research thesis.
courses: Intellectual Property and its Management in Agriculture
Agricultural Research, Research Ethics and Rural Development Programmes

practical_learning.name: Thesis research
practical_learning.description: Each student plans and runs an experiment, often on the university research farm, under an advisor and advisory committee, then writes and defends a thesis.

practical_learning.name: Practical classes
practical_learning.description: Most agronomy courses carry practical credits covering field layout, nutrient and water budgeting, weed surveys and crop growth measurements.

practical_learning.name: Master's seminar
practical_learning.description: A one-credit seminar in which the student reviews recent literature on a topic and presents it to the department.

points: A bachelor's degree in agriculture, normally the four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture; some universities and the ICAR bulletin also accept certain allied degrees for agronomy, so check the subject-wise eligibility list for the admission year.

A minimum overall grade point average or percentage in the bachelor's degree, with relaxation for reserved categories; the threshold is set in the ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and in each university's prospectus.
For ICAR quota seats, the bachelor's degree is generally expected to be from an institution and programme that meet ICAR's norms; requirements vary, so confirm in the current bulletin.
Final-year students can usually apply provisionally but must show the completed degree by the date the admitting university specifies.

routes.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
routes.description: A national entrance test conducted by NTA on behalf of ICAR. Its merit list is used for ICAR's all-India quota seats in agricultural universities and for ICAR PG scholarships. Candidates choose a major subject group; Agronomy has its own group.

routes.name: State agricultural university entrance or merit
routes.description: Seats outside the ICAR quota in state agricultural universities are filled through the university's or state's own entrance test, interview or merit process, which differs by state.

routes.name: Private and other universities
routes.description: Private universities that follow the ICAR syllabus usually run their own entrance test or admit on merit; procedures and seat numbers are set by each institution.

exams.name: ICAR AIEEA (PG)
exams.note: Computer-based multiple-choice test in the chosen subject group. Secondary reports of recent cycles describe 120 questions in 2 hours with negative marking; confirm the pattern in that year's information bulletin.

steps.title: Check subject-wise eligibility
steps.text: Read the current ICAR AIEEA (PG) bulletin and your target universities' prospectuses to confirm that your bachelor's degree qualifies for agronomy.

steps.title: Register for the entrance
steps.text: Apply online for ICAR AIEEA (PG) under the Agronomy subject group and for any state or university entrance you also intend to take.

steps.title: Take the test and follow counselling
steps.text: After results, register for ICAR online counselling or the relevant university counselling and fill in university and subject choices.

steps.title: Report for admission
steps.text: Complete document verification and fee payment at the allotted university within the notified dates.

fees.summary: Fees for M.Sc. Agronomy vary widely. State agricultural universities usually charge much less than private universities, and some universities charge different amounts to ICAR quota, state quota, out-of-state and NRI or management seats. Hostel and examination charges are often billed separately. Students admitted through ICAR AIEEA (PG) may be eligible for an ICAR PG scholarship under that year's rules. Check the current fee notice of the admitting university.

careers.heading: Where an agronomy master's can lead
careers.intro: Agronomy postgraduates work wherever crop production decisions are made: in research stations, extension systems, input companies and farm advisory services. Many continue to a Ph.D. Government routes usually need separate competitive exams, so the degree is a qualification for applying rather than a guarantee of selection.

roles.title: Research associate or senior research fellow
roles.description: Supports field trials on crop varieties, nutrients, irrigation or weed control in ICAR institutes, universities or funded projects.

roles.title: Agronomist in agri-input or seed companies
roles.description: Plans demonstration plots and advises farmers and dealers on crop management for the company's products.

roles.title: Subject matter specialist (agronomy)
roles.description: Delivers crop production training and on-farm trials, for example at Krishi Vigyan Kendras, subject to recruitment rules.

roles.title: Farm or plantation manager
roles.description: Manages crop planning, input use and labour on large farms, estates or contract-farming operations.

roles.title: Assistant professor or scientist (with further qualifications)
roles.description: Teaching and research posts generally also require qualifying ASRB or UGC NET and often a Ph.D.

sectors: Seeds, fertilisers and crop protection industry
public_sector_routes: ASRB NET (Agronomy) for lecturer or assistant professor eligibility in agricultural universities
ASRB Agricultural Research Service (ARS) examination for scientist posts in ICAR
State public service commission agriculture officer recruitment
IBPS Agricultural Field Officer (Specialist Officer) recruitment
higher_study: Ph.D. in allied areas such as Agricultural Meteorology, Water Science or Organic Farming where eligibility allows

skills: Designing and laying out field experiments and analysing them statistically
Planning nutrient, irrigation and weed management for different crops and seasons
Assessing cropping and farming systems for productivity and sustainability
Using GIS, remote sensing and crop simulation tools at an introductory level
Writing technical reports and presenting research findings

faqs.question: Who is eligible for M.Sc. Agronomy?
faqs.answer: Normally graduates of the four-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture. Some universities and the ICAR bulletin list additional allied degrees, and a minimum grade point average applies, so check the current subject-wise eligibility rules.

faqs.question: Which entrance exam do I need?
faqs.answer: ICAR AIEEA (PG), run by NTA, is used for ICAR quota seats and ICAR PG scholarships. Other seats are filled through state or university entrance tests or merit, depending on the institution.

faqs.question: How long is the course and how is it structured?
faqs.answer: Two years over four semesters. Under the ICAR framework, students earn 70 credits: 40 from major, minor, supporting and common courses plus a seminar, and 30 from thesis research.

faqs.question: Is a thesis compulsory?
faqs.answer: Yes. Thesis research carries 30 of the 70 credits in the ICAR framework, and the student must submit and defend a thesis before the degree is awarded.

faqs.question: What jobs can I apply for after M.Sc. Agronomy?
faqs.answer: Research project positions, agronomist roles in seed and input companies, farm management and extension roles, and government posts through competitive exams such as state agriculture officer or IBPS AFO recruitment.

faqs.question: Can I do a Ph.D. after this degree?
faqs.answer: Yes. Ph.D. Agronomy admissions in agricultural universities use ICAR AICE-JRF/SRF (Ph.D.) for ICAR seats and fellowships, along with university-level processes.
